what_this_is: A made-up sales page and a made-up video script, and the rule rows a person might keep for them. The page holds exactly six long dashes, three hedges ('hoping') and four weak intensifiers ('very'); the script has a hook, two authority lines and a credibility line, and no quote and no ask, so a script rule set that needs all five parts finds exactly those two missing.

blocks.text: Learn to throw a pot in one weekend
You have watched the videos—and you are still hoping the clay will behave.
This class is very hands-on. You sit at a wheel from the first hour—not at a desk.
Most beginners are hoping for one good bowl. Most leave with three, and a very full shelf.
Glazes, tools and firing—all on us
It is very simple: come curious, leave with clay on your sleeves. No more hoping.
A very first bowl, still wet—and already lopsided in the right way.

rules.says: Long dashes are not used in page words.
A short dash: prefer a hyphen or rewrite.
Say it as a plain claim.
Cut it or use a stronger word.

blocks.text: Nine out of ten people get these three things wrong when they first sit at a wheel.
Everyone talks about pressing harder. The first thing is, you do not press at all. You let the wheel do the work and keep your hands still.
The next thing is water. Too little and the clay drags; too much and it slumps. Keep it just wet enough to shine.
Do both and look: the walls rise on their own, and the third thing, a slow wheel, keeps them true.

rules.says: A script has a hook, authority, credibility, a quote and an ask.
The parts come hook, authority, credibility, quote, ask.
The hook is long for a three-second open.
Long dashes are not used in script words.
Say it as a plain claim.
